notes: Closest match to MEC-11. Commission 2025: "the limitation in the use of e-government services generated by a still low demand (especially in rural areas)"; "Over 50% of services mapped for businesses and individuals are (fully or partially) available digitally". Measures: EVO app and portal, 105 assisted public service centres (CUPS), e-signature (over 266 000 users, 10% of adults). Headline check: the e-Governance Agency reports 445 of 636 services digital (70%) and 71% of requests online in January to June 2026, but this is government data, and the definition counts partly automated services. The Commission figure is lower. IPRE (2023, from AGE and ministry data): only 36 of 157 requestable services were fully digital, and 128 of 226 reported digital services (56.63%) had zero users in 2022. No independent check after 2022 found; the 71% figure is unverified. Moldova is not in the Western Balkans DESI. SIGMA material not checked.
recommend: yes: same issue and mechanism; use is measured service by service, which is rare; mixed outcome with a usable test of the headline

notes: Opposite profile: high use, thin depth, unequal access. Commission 2025: "95% of applications for 1 253 public services were offered online"; "There is a need to address the emerging digital divide and strengthen the ability of citizens to independently use e-services"; recommendation to "improve access to the use of e-services". It fits the "does not serve all users" limb of the definition, not low use. Reform: mandatory digital-first delivery through e-Albania (Law 43/2023). Headline check: the 95% measures services offered online, not completed end to end, and I found no independent audit of it (World Bank and Commission restate it; the World Bank +40% requests 2023 to 2025 is not independently checked). WB DESI 2025: users 78.5% to 88.6% (highest in WB6) but citizen services score 36 (2023) to 50 (2025), below the WB6 average of 53: "Despite the breadth and intensity of service use, Albania continues to lag ... in certain aspects of service scope and sophistication". IDM PAR Monitor: e-payment "usually it does not work" (footnote 64), which sits awkwardly with its own text that two sampled services are end to end. Press reports paid intermediaries (not checked). High use may reflect compulsion, so it cannot be read as demand. The 2019 audit by the supreme audit institution was reachable only as a failed slide page, and is outside the window; SIGMA 2024 returned 403.
recommend: yes: tests whether mandating the portal fixes use, and at what cost; reputation as regional leader is not supported on depth

notes: Closest EU wording on transactional depth. Commission 2025 recommendation: "prioritise the development and implementation of an interactive e-government platform for transactional electronic services"; also "there was no noticeable improvement in the quality and the number of e-services available as of the end of 2023" and "poor planning and no effective collection of key data". Mechanisms lean to coordination, capacity and data rather than MEC-11 alone. Reform: new portal launched December 2024, first e-services April 2025, plan for 171 by 2027; "just 4 out of 37 of the plan's activities completed". WB DESI 2025: users 48.4% to 37.5% (the only WB6 fall). Institut Alternativa event report: none of seven essential sampled services on the portal; a UNDP speaker said 52% know of e-services and 8% use them. The 8% and 37.5% conflict, and measure different things: report it, do not resolve it. Confound: the 2023 cyberattack. Reform is recent, so outcome evidence is short. SIGMA 2024 not reached.
recommend: yes: a stalled case with the same starting point as North Macedonia, kept to avoid selecting only on progress; close call because the outcome window is short

notes: Close call. Commission 2025: "Service delivery to citizens and businesses, in particular e-services, is continuously improving. Further developments are hampered by the fragmentation of responsibilities and mandates among institutions and the lack of a dedicated coordination system." No EU wording on low use found. WB DESI 2025: users 52.4% to 58.5%, citizen services score 62 to 69, highest in WB6. The national PAR Monitor (CEP, read from a copy already fetched in this session; the URL was not captured) cites fragmented platforms and "insufficient promotion" and says property registration and VAT payment are not online. No portal-level usage or transaction counts found. Government claims of regional leadership rest on SIGMA, whose 2024 report returned 403, so I could not check them. Much of the fragmentation problem belongs to RI-TEC-037, not this issue.
recommend: no: reasonable relative performer, but issue framing is coordination and no usable use data were reached; first reserve if SIGMA 2024 shows use data

notes: Member state, so no enlargement report in the window; pre-accession reports are out of time. Digital Decade 2026: "Digital public services also remain uneven" and recommends "accelerating end-to-end digitalisation". Citizen services score 67.2 to 75.2 (2025 report table), against a 2025 EU figure of 82.3. Ministerial claims of 2.085 million e-Citizens users and 100 000 mGradani users are not independently checked and count accounts, not transactions. A ministry release says use is above the EU average; no Eurostat figure for Croatia was retrieved, and older academic papers describe low use. Problem is depth and interoperability, not low use.
recommend: no: mechanism differs, no comparable EU framing, and use evidence is only ministerial
